headline: Approved Certificates of Compliance for nine properties, a tree removal, two deck/turf projects, and an Order of Conditions for 76 & 78 Paine Avenue
summary: The Commission issued Certificates of Compliance for multiple properties including 4 Upland Road, 57 Beaver Pond Road, 2 Thaxton Road, 12 Museum Road, 662 Cabot Street, 19R & 21 Linden Avenue, 5 Curtis Point, 32 Haskell Street, and 4 Bridle Path Lane. It approved a tree removal request at 565 Hale Street, issued Negative 3 Determinations of Applicability for projects at 21 Wirling Drive and 451 Essex Street, and issued an Order of Conditions for 76 & 78 Paine Avenue. The Commission also approved mileage expenditures and the August 18, 2026 meeting minutes.
decisions: Issued a Complete Certificate of Compliance for 4 Upland Road, DEP File #5-1422, 4-0.
Issued a Partial Certificate of Compliance for 57 Beaver Pond Road, DEP File #5-702, 4-0.
Issued a Complete Certificate of Compliance for 2 Thaxton Road, DEP File #5-1359, 4-0.
Issued a Complete Certificate of Compliance for 12 Museum Road, DEP File #5-1293, 4-0.

Issued a Complete Certificate of Compliance for 19R & 21 Linden Avenue, DEP File #5-1375, 4-0.
Issued a Complete Certificate of Compliance for 5 Curtis Point, DEP File #5-1431, 4-0.
Issued a Complete Certificate of Compliance for 32 Haskell Street, DEP File #5-1444, 4-0.
Issued a Complete Certificate of Compliance for 4 Bridle Path Lane, DEP File #5-1361, 4-0.
Approved the tree removal request at 565 Hale Street with conditions, 4-0.
Closed the public hearing for 76 & 78 Paine Avenue, DEP File #5-1479, 4-0.
Issued a Negative 3 Determination of Applicability with conditions for 21 Wirling Drive, 4-0.
Issued a Negative 3 Determination of Applicability with conditions for 451 Essex Street, 4-0.
Approved payment of Conservation Agent August mileage of $15.88 and Conservation Field Inspector August mileage of $36.45, 4-0.
Issued an Order of Conditions for 76 & 78 Paine Avenue, DEP File #5-1479, 4-0.
Approved the meeting minutes of August 18, 2026, as amended, 3-0-1.

Jesse Blanchette, Griffin Engineering, explains that there have been a few changes to the project. 206 
On the northeast side of the proposed residence, a lawn service path has been braided in. The 207

approximately 3’. This has a trickle-down effect of raising the pool terrace area as well. There 212

propane tanks will be moved to the west of the garage. This is outside of the buffer zone and 215

been coordinated so that all of the downspouts will run into robust infiltration beds. A comment 217 
from DEP was received and is similar to a comment received from the abutters at 75 Paine Ave. 218 
The DEP comment reads that “the proponent should evaluate if the proposed project and filling 219 
will change flow characteristics, redirecting it onto adjacent properties, or increase the volume 220 
and velocity of flow”. The applicant responded to DEP with the revised plans noting a 221 
comparison of pre-construction and proposed impervious surfaces, resulting in a net decrease of 222 
1,200 s.f. from the proposed redevelopment. Also, the applicant will provide substantially more 223 
on-site infiltration. The preconstruction drainage system included a couple of dry wells in a 224

1. Erosion and sedimentation control devices shall be installed along the  314 
  edge of the down gradient side of the project area prior to construction as  315
